content:
Mei Lin: collecting region normalization edge cases here — places where region labels differ across gateway/runtime/infra billing sources. pls reply w/ exact strings you’ve seen + where they came from. goal is to finalize mapping table + guardrails so aggregates stop dropping rows.

Nadia Rahman: from token metering (gateway): we currently emit `region=us-east-1` for most hosted, but I’ve seen `us_east_1` in older events (pre Dec) coming from a legacy env var. also some requests have `region=iad` when they go through the colo POP path.

Allison Grant: +1 on `iad`. in metrics pipeline, we also see `us-east` (no suffix) from the runtime sidecar in private clusters. pretty sure that’s from `RW_REGION=us-east` (someone set it manually).

Cole Summers: infra billing inputs:
- AWS CUR uses “US East (N. Virginia)” + “EU (Ireland)” etc (human names)
- GCP export uses `us-central1` etc (ok)
- our colo vendor invoice has `IAD1`, `SJC1`, `FRA1` (site codes)
We need mapping for both “provider region” and “internal site”. finance rate card currently keyed by provider+region, not site.

Sean Gallagher: SRE incident last week was because we started treating unknown region as null -> then aggregator did inner join on region dim and dropped rows. we need an explicit `unknown` bucket and an alert when it’s > X%.

Logan Wright: can we enumerate runtime labels? I remember `use1` showing up in the dedicated k8s clusters.

Jada Williams: yep. from serving runtime request context:
- `use1`, `usw2`, `euw1` (short codes) in some older dedicated deployments
- also `eu-west-1` comes through as `eu-west-1a` sometimes (!!) because someone passes availability zone instead of region
- and I’ve seen `aws/us-east-1` prefixed strings in the router logs

Caleb Johnson: for completeness checks, we can’t just do “region not null” — we need to validate against the canonical list. I’m seeing the following in warehouse raw events (sampled last 7d):
`us-east-1`, `us_east_1`, `use1`, `us-east`, `iad`, `IAD1`, `aws/us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `eu-west-1a`, `EU (Ireland)`, `unknown`, ``(empty string)
Also: `us-west-2 ` with a trailing space (seriously).

Felix Schneider: UI side question: do we want to display “US East (N. Virginia)” or `us-east-1`? Product asked for “friendly labels” but drilldowns should be stable for filters.

Mei Lin: for v1 I’d prefer canonical id = provider region (`aws:us-east-1`) and friendly display separate. warehouse dims can keep both, API returns display_name. (but we need to decide for colo)

Cole Summers: colo is tricky because it’s not 1:1 to cloud regions. finance allocates colo costs by “site” (IAD1/FRA1/etc) but product wants “region” rolled up like `us-east` / `eu-central`. Maybe canonical should be `region_id` (geo) and `site_id` (colo). rate card can map site -> geo region.

Nadia Rahman: +1 to two-level. from metering perspective, I can add both `region` and `site` dims but need to keep cardinality sane. `site` only for colo, else null.

Allison Grant: careful: private deployments in customer VPCs sometimes set region to the customer’s cloud region (e.g. `eu-central-1`) but those should still roll up under tier=private. we should ensure region normalization doesn’t accidentally collapse hosted+private when finance wants separate tier cut.

Logan Wright: agreed. region normalization should be orthogonal to tier mapping. but we also need region to reconcile to spend inputs. for private, we won’t have our own spend by customer VPC region (it’s their infra), so it should probably land in an “excluded from blended” bucket? (or $=0 depending on methodology).

Mei Lin: yep — ADR says blended metric is for Redwood-served infra only (hosted + dedicated + Redwood-operated private). customer-managed private is excluded from blended numerator/denominator but still can show usage. separate issue, but region dims still should normalize.

Jada Williams: more edge cases:
- azure: `westeurope` (no dash) coming from one pilot
- internal: `eu-west` used as a *geo* bucket (not provider-specific)

Caleb Johnson: can we lock down allowed values at ingestion? e.g. normalize `us_east_1` -> `us-east-1`, strip whitespace, drop AZ suffix (`eu-west-1a` -> `eu-west-1`) and parse prefixes (`aws/us-east-1`). anything else -> `unknown` + emit counter metric.

Sean Gallagher: yes please. also log sample of unknown raw value for debugging but don’t put raw strings into high-cardinality tags.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: for “unknown_raw_value” sampled logs only. We got burned by tag explosions.

Quentin Harris: model metadata side: we also have “region” in model catalog benchmarks (e.g. `us-east-1`), but those are *benchmark location* not request region. Just flagging to avoid someone joining the wrong table later.

Mei Lin: good call. I’ll name the dim `request_region_id` / `request_site_id` in warehouse views to avoid confusion.

Felix Schneider: what about multi-region strings? I saw `us-east-1,us-west-2` once in an internal load test config.

Nadia Rahman: that’s from the gateway client setting fallback regions; shouldn’t be in per-request metering. If it is, that’s a bug—per-request should be the actual region served.

Jada Williams: +1, per-request should be resolved post-routing. if you see comma-separated, it’s likely being pulled from config not runtime. I can track down.

Mei Lin: action items (reply if wrong):
1) Mei: draft mapping table w/ canonical ids + display names; include parser rules (trim, prefix strip, AZ->region) + explicit unknown bucket.
2) Jada: investigate comma-separated + `aws/us-east-1` prefixes; fix at source if possible.
3) Nadia/Allison: confirm where `use1/usw2/euw1` shortcodes are set; either migrate env vars or normalize at ingestion.
4) Cole: provide finance-approved mapping of colo sites (IAD1/FRA1/etc) -> geo region + rate card keys.
5) Sean/Caleb: define alert threshold for unknown region rate + missing mapping coverage.

Logan Wright: looks right. one more: please include “US East (N. Virginia)” and “EU (Ireland)” mappings from CUR; those are the main reconciliation pain.

Cole Summers: will send the list from the last CUR export. also note: AWS sometimes has “Europe (Frankfurt)” but we want `eu-central-1`. same for “Asia Pacific (Tokyo)” -> `ap-northeast-1`.

Sean Gallagher: can we make sure joins are left joins in aggregation until mapping is 100%? dropping data silently is the worst.

Mei Lin: yep. we’ll do left join + `unknown` canonical row; then completeness check gates can yell at us instead of losing rows.

Caleb Johnson: :+1: I’ll update data quality spec to treat `unknown` as valid but alert when it exceeds baseline.

Mei Lin: cool. I’ll post the mapping draft in this thread later today.

Mei Lin: update: mapping draft started. current rules:
- `trim(lower(region_raw))`
- strip prefixes `aws/`, `gcp/`, `azure/`
- map short codes: `use1->us-east-1`, `usw2->us-west-2`, `euw1->eu-west-1`
- if matches `^[a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-\d[a-z]$` (AZ), drop last char
- map CUR names: `us east (n. virginia)->us-east-1`, `eu (ireland)->eu-west-1`, etc
Anything else => `unknown`
Still need colo site mapping from Cole.

Cole Summers: got it. colo mapping proposal:
- `IAD1` -> geo `us-east`
- `SJC1` -> geo `us-west`
- `FRA1` -> geo `eu-central`
We don’t have provider region equivalents for colo, so suggest canonical `site_id` for colo + a derived `geo_region` for rollups.

Allison Grant: works. pls make sure geo_region is a small fixed set (`us-east`, `us-west`, `eu-west`, `eu-central`, `ap-southeast`, etc). don’t want a new dimension explosion.

Mei Lin: ack. closing loop here once I bake in colo + update PR for mapping table.

Sean Gallagher: thanks. once merged, let’s also backfill the last 7d to make sure finance doesn’t see a step-function from “unknown” dropping to real regions.

Mei Lin: noted. will coordinate backfill window w/ SRE (don’t want to slam the warehouse again).
